Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 103, verses 1–3:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–3} Allah, exalted is He, swears by al-'Asr (the time), which is the night and the day, the place of the actions and deeds of the servants, that every human being is in loss. The one who suffers loss is the opposite of the one who profits, and loss has multiple, varying degrees. At times it is absolute loss, like the state of one who has lost this world and the Hereafter, whose bliss is lost and who deserves the Blazing Fire.

At other times a person is a loser in some respects but not in others. For this reason Allah made loss general to every human being, except for those who possess four qualities:

Faith (iman) in what Allah has commanded belief in. Faith cannot exist without knowledge ('ilm); it is a branch of knowledge that cannot be complete without it.

And righteous deeds, which encompass all acts of goodness, outward and inward, relating to the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants, obligatory and recommended.

And mutual counsel to truth, which is faith and righteous deeds; that is, some of them advise one another to these, urge one another toward them, and encourage one another to them.

And mutual counsel to patience: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah, and patience in the painful decrees of Allah. By the first two matters the servant perfects himself, and by the last two he perfects others. And by perfecting these four matters, the servant will have been saved from loss and will have attained the great profit.
